senses.definition: A car you pay to ride in, also called a taxi.
senses.example: We got a cab from the station to the museum.

senses.definition: The part of a truck or train where the driver sits.
senses.example: The driver climbed into the truck cab.

senses.definition: A vegetable with broad leaves, often forming a firm round bunch.
senses.example: We chopped a cabbage to make a crunchy salad.

senses.definition: A small, simple house, often in the woods.
senses.example: We stayed in a cabin near the lake.

senses.definition: An enclosed area for people in a ship, airplane, or other vehicle.
senses.example: An attendant checked the airplane cabin before takeoff.

senses.definition: A bridge with cables running directly between its towers and points along the roadway or path.
senses.example: The cables of the cable-stayed bridge spread out like fans.

senses.definition: A place that keeps a copy of information so a computer may use it again quickly.
senses.example: The browser could read the image from its cache.

senses.definition: A plant with a thick stem that can store water, often with sharp spines instead of leaves.
senses.example: The cactus near the path had a bright pink flower.

senses.definition: A small protective cover some young caddisflies make using silk and material from the stream or pond around them.
senses.example: The caddisfly case was made with tiny grains of sand.

senses.definition: A place where people choose food from a counter and carry it to a table to eat.
senses.example: We ate lunch in the school cafeteria.

senses.definition: A container fenced in by bars or wire, often used for animals.
senses.example: The vet put a towel inside the travel cage.

senses.definition: To keep someone or something behind bars or wire.

senses.definition: An event that brings great trouble or damage.
senses.example: Losing all its stored grain in a flood was a calamity for the village.

senses.definition: An element that is part of strong bones and teeth and helps nerves and muscles do their jobs.
senses.example: The nutrition label shows that the yogurt provides calcium.

senses.definition: To work out a number or amount by using math.
senses.example: We used a ruler and multiplication to calculate the area.

senses.definition: An electronic tool or program that works out answers to math problems.
senses.example: I used a calculator to check my total.

senses.definition: A chart or computer tool that shows days, weeks, and months.
senses.example: We marked the first day of camp on the calendar.

senses.definition: To speak loudly to get someone’s attention, or to reach someone by phone.
senses.example: Please call me when the game is over.

senses.definition: To give or use a name for someone or something.
senses.example: We call our cat Button.

senses.definition: An attempt to reach someone by phone or a shout to get attention.
senses.example: I missed a call from my aunt.

senses.definition: To decide you have done enough for the day and stop.
senses.example: We had painted the whole first wall, so we decided to call it a day.

senses.definition: Letters or numbers that tell you where an item belongs in a library collection.
senses.example: I wrote down the call number before I went to find the book on its shelf.

senses.definition: To cancel something that was planned.
senses.example: The organizers called off the game when the field flooded.

senses.definition: To say something loudly so others can hear it.
senses.example: I called out my name so my group could find me.

senses.definition: Lettering written with care as a form of art.
senses.example: The invitation was decorated with blue calligraphy.

senses.definition: Quiet, still, or free from strong worry.
senses.example: The lake was so calm that we could see clouds in it.

senses.definition: To make someone or something less upset or active.
senses.example: Music helped calm the nervous puppy.

senses.definition: The breaking away of ice from the edge of a glacier to form floating pieces.

senses.definition: A large animal with long legs and one or two humps on its back.
senses.example: A camel walked quietly across the sand.

senses.definition: A device that takes photos or records a moving picture.
senses.example: The camera caught a picture of a bird in flight.

senses.definition: A dark space where light through a small opening makes a picture on a surface inside.
senses.example: A camera obscura showed an upside-down picture of the trees outside.

senses.definition: Color, shape, or pattern that makes a living thing hard to see in a place.

senses.definition: A place or program where people stay or spend time doing things together, often outdoors.
senses.example: We made kites at day camp.

senses.definition: To stay outdoors for a while, often sleeping in a tent.
senses.example: Our family likes to camp by the lake.

senses.definition: A place where people set up a tent or sleep in a camping vehicle.
senses.example: We picked a flat campsite with room for two tents.

entries.pronunciation: kan (container), kan or kuhn (be able to)

senses.definition: To be able, allowed, or free to do something.
senses.example: I can read the sign from here.

senses.definition: A metal container that holds food, drink, or something else.
senses.example: I found a can of beans on the shelf.

senses.definition: To seal food in a container to keep it for later.
senses.example: We can peaches to eat in winter.

senses.definition: A waterway made by people to carry boats or to move water.

senses.definition: A small singing bird that is often yellow when kept as a pet.
senses.example: The canary sang when we opened the curtains.

senses.definition: To decide that a planned event or order will stop or will no longer happen.
senses.example: The coach had to cancel practice because of lightning.

senses.definition: A piece of wax with a string through it that can be lit to give light.
senses.example: The candle on the cake had a tiny flame.

senses.definition: A sweet food that comes in pieces or bars, often made with sugar or chocolate.
senses.example: I saved one piece of candy for my sister.

senses.definition: A large, heavy gun, often seen in museums, historic forts, or history books.
senses.example: We read a sign beside the old cannon at the fort.

senses.definition: A heavy ball that was fired from a cannon in the past.
senses.example: The museum displayed a round iron cannonball.

senses.definition: A way of jumping into water with your knees tucked in so you make a splash.

senses.definition: A long narrow boat moved using paddles held in the hands.

senses.definition: To travel in a canoe.
senses.example: We canoed slowly around the lake’s shallow edge.

senses.definition: A small container for carrying drinking water.

senses.definition: A place in a school, camp, or workplace where people can get food or drinks.

senses.definition: A strong, heavy cloth used for things such as bags, tents, and paintings.

senses.definition: A deep valley with steep sides, often with a river at the bottom.

senses.definition: A soft hat, a cover for a small opening, or a limit on how large something can be.

senses.example: Our teacher capped the team size at six.

senses.definition: Having the ability to do a certain thing.
senses.example: My little brother is capable of making his own sandwich now.

senses.definition: A device that stores energy by keeping opposite electric charges apart.

senses.definition: How much a thing or place can hold.

senses.definition: The ability or power to do something.

senses.definition: Clothing that hangs down from the shoulders without sleeves.

senses.definition: A piece of land that sticks out into water.

senses.definition: A tiny tube where materials can pass between blood and nearby tissue.

senses.definition: The city or town where a country’s or state’s main government is based.
senses.example: Boston is the capital of Massachusetts.

senses.definition: An uppercase form of a letter, such as A instead of a.

senses.definition: Money or property available to start or run a business.

senses.definition: Written words that help explain a picture or tell what you would hear in a video.

senses.definition: A sweet food or flavor made from sugar heated until it turns golden brown.

senses.definition: A hard covering over all or part of an animal’s back.

senses.definition: A group of travelers who make part of a trip together, often carrying goods.
senses.example: The caravan carried salt across the desert.

senses.definition: A type of material that includes sugars, starches, and many kinds of fiber.
senses.example: Oatmeal contains more than one kind of carbohydrate.

senses.example: Carbon dioxide moves from the blood into the air inside your lungs.

senses.definition: A flat piece of stiff paper, thin plastic, or similar material that may hold information or be used in a game.
senses.example: I signed my name at the bottom of the card.

senses.definition: Thick paper or layers of paper used for things such as boxes and folders.
senses.example: We made a bridge from strips of cardboard.

senses.definition: To feel concern or interest for someone or something.

senses.definition: Attention or help given to keep someone or something safe or well.
senses.example: Our neighbor took care of the cat while we were away.

senses.definition: Attention to how you do something so you avoid trouble or mistakes.
senses.example: Carry the full bowl with care.

senses.definition: Paying attention to avoid mistakes, trouble, or harm.
senses.example: Be careful when you turn the corner with the full tray.

senses.definition: Not giving enough attention to what you are doing.
senses.example: I made a careless mistake by writing my answer on the wrong line.

senses.definition: Goods carried by a ship, airplane, truck, or train.
senses.example: The ship’s cargo included boxes of oranges.

senses.definition: Adapted to get food or nutrients by eating animals.

senses.definition: Someone whose job is building or repairing things made of wood.

senses.definition: A heavy piece of woven material that covers some or all of a floor.
senses.example: I sat on the carpet beside the bookcase.

senses.definition: To cover a floor or surface like a carpet.

senses.definition: A wheeled vehicle, especially one pulled by a horse.
senses.example: The wheels of the carriage rattled over the stones.

senses.definition: A passenger car in a train.

senses.definition: To hold or support something while taking it from one place to another.

senses.definition: To have, hold, or pass something along.

senses.definition: A tough, bendy body material found in places such as your ears and joints.

senses.definition: A funny or simple drawing, or a show made with moving drawings or digital images.
senses.example: The cartoon showed a duck wearing a tiny hat.

senses.definition: To cut into something to make a shape, design, or slices.

senses.definition: Money in the form of bills or coins.

senses.definition: To exchange a check or similar paper for money.

senses.definition: A building or group of buildings made with strong walls to protect people, especially in the past.

senses.definition: An organized list of items, such as books in a library or products for sale.

senses.example: The class cataloged the objects by shape and color.

senses.definition: To stop and hold something that is moving through the air or trying to get away.

senses.definition: To arrive in time to get on a bus, train, or other ride.

senses.definition: To figure out how something works or what someone means.

senses.definition: An aim that people work to support.

senses.definition: To make something happen.

senses.definition: Care taken to avoid a mistake or danger.

senses.definition: A place where a particular activity happens or services are offered.
senses.example: The town opened a new community center.

senses.definition: A hard material, such as fired clay, usually made from minerals and set by heat.

senses.definition: Food made from grain, often eaten with milk for breakfast.

senses.definition: An opportunity to do something.

senses.definition: Luck or something that happens without a plan.

senses.definition: One letter, number, symbol, or other mark in a line of text.

senses.definition: To ask someone to pay a price for something.

senses.definition: To put energy into a battery so it can be used again.

senses.definition: To rush forward quickly.

senses.definition: A quality that makes someone or something pleasant or appealing.
